nodes.question: What are the financial implications of rabies prevention and control in the US?
nodes.answer: Billions of US dollars are forfeited annually for rabies prevention and control measures in response to rabies outbreaks caused by bats.
nodes.paragraph: Low-income countries in the tropics are even more vulnerable to bat- 1Translational Biology, Medicine, and Health Program, Virginia Tech Graduate School, Blacksburg, VA, USA. 2Department of Fish and Wildlife Conservation, Virginia Tech, Blacksburg, VA 24061, USA. 3Center for Emerging Zoonotic and Arthropod-borne Pathogens, Virginia Tech, Blacksburg, VA, USA. 4Department of Population Health Sciences, Virginia Tech, Blacksburg, VA, USA. 5Global Change Center, Virginia Tech, Blacksburg, VA, USA. email: escobar1@vt.edu OPEN Scientific Reports www.nature.com/scientificreports borne emerging diseases due to compounding risk factors29,30. The study of future climate change impacts to the distribution of bats is, therefore, critically important for both human and animal health. Nevertheless, research in the tropics on this topic has been scarce to date31. In Latin America, rabies virus (RABV) is a well-documented and impactful bat-borne pathogen26,32. Thousands of cattle are lost to bat-borne rabies in Latin America annually33 35, and billions of United States (US) dollars are forfeit annually for rabies prevention and control measures36.
